root_cause.text: `extract_kvec_to_sg()` in `lib/scatterlist.c` misused the remaining segment length when building scatterlist entries from a kvec, allowing `sg_set_page()` to be given a length that could span past a page boundary and leaving the returned byte count inconsistent when the sg list ran out of entries.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `sg_set_page(sg, page, len, off)` to `sg_set_page(sg, page, seg, off)`, with the commit message stating “do not cross page boundaries” because “The required length was already calculated but not used as intended,” and it adds `ret -= len;` plus an early `if (maxsize == 0 || sg_max == 0) return 0;` to handle incomplete extraction and empty sg lists.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix scatter-gather entry sizing in `extract_kvec_to_sg()` by using the segment length instead of the local length value.
intent_record.what: In `extract_kvec_to_sg()`, the third argument passed to `sg_set_page()` was changed from `len` to `seg` while keeping the same `page` and `off` arguments.
intent_record.how: This alters the size recorded in each scatter-gather entry from the local `len` value to the segment length `seg`, which changes how much data each SG entry represents at runtime and likely corrects incorrect SG sizing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the return value tracking in `extract_kvec_to_sg()` so partially unprocessed data is properly reflected in the result.
intent_record.what: A new statement `ret -= len;` was inserted in `extract_kvec_to_sg()` after the inner `do/while` loop and before the check of `maxsize` and `sg_max`.
intent_record.how: This changes the function’s accounting of the return value by subtracting any remaining unprocessed length from `ret`, so the function reports less data as successfully extracted when the loop exits before consuming everything.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early guard to return immediately when the scatter-gather entry limit is zero.
intent_record.what: The function `extract_iter_to_sg()` changed its early return condition from `if (maxsize == 0)` to `if (maxsize == 0 || sg_max == 0)`, so it now exits immediately when either the requested maximum size is zero or the scatter-gather entry limit is zero.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will no longer attempt to extract data into a scatter-gather table when no SG entries are allowed, preventing invalid or pointless processing in that case and returning 0 consistently.

Fix the return value tracking in `extract_kvec_to_sg()` so partially unprocessed data is properly reflected in the result.
Add an early guard to return immediately when the scatter-gather entry limit is zero.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes `extract_kvec_to_sg()` scatterlist entry sizing by using the correct segment length, which addresses the bad length calculation that could cross page boundaries and cause inconsistent byte counts.

The change is directly about `extract_kvec_to_sg()` and fixes how the function tracks and returns partially processed data when the scatterlist fills up, which matches part of the stated root cause involving inconsistent returned byte counts.

The change only adds an early return when the scatter-gather entry limit is zero. It does not address the kvec-to-sg length calculation, page-boundary handling, or byte-count inconsistency described in the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the directly vulnerable call: it passes the remaining length variable into sg_set_page() rather than the per-segment length, which can create an sg entry that spans beyond a page boundary.

This condition governs when the function stops after running out of sg entries or space; the bug description notes that the returned byte count becomes inconsistent when the sg list runs out of entries.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the root-cause bug: it uses the remaining segment length variable when setting each scatterlist entry, instead of the per-page chunk length. That can make an sg entry extend past a page boundary in extract_kvec_to_sg().

This stop condition is tied to the incorrect accounting for how many bytes were actually consumed. When the sg list runs out of entries or space, the function's returned byte count can become inconsistent with the data left unprocessed.

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the shown function body is sufficient because it contains the full KVEC extraction logic in question. The vulnerable construct is present in `extract_kvec_to_sg()`: it computes `seg = min_t(size_t, len, PAGE_SIZE - off);` but then calls `sg_set_page(sg, page, len, off);` instead of using `seg`. That means the scatterlist entry length can exceed the remaining bytes in the current page and can span past a page boundary, matching the root cause. The code also decrements `len -= seg;` and advances `kaddr += PAGE_SIZE;`, so the intended split across pages is clear, but the `sg_set_page()` argument is still the full `len`, not the per-page `seg`. There is no fix here: no corrected `sg_set_page(..., seg, off)` and no special handling for the case where the sg list runs out of entries to keep the returned byte count consistent.
